text: Installing Pollis and Julia, the first launch, and how the Julia packages a panel needs are installed. Pollis is a single application with no account and no licence key. It writes Julia code; Julia, which runs that code, is installed separately, from the Welcome page, in a few minutes.

Download the file for your system from github.com/saragga/pollis/releases/latest. macOS (Apple silicon), Pollis-darwin-arm64.zip: Unzip it and move Pollis.app to Applications. In Terminal, run xattr -cr /Applications/Pollis.app. Open Pollis. Windows (x64), PollisSetup-x64.exe: Double-click it. If SmartScreen warns you, choose More info, then Run anyway. Click Install. No administrator rights are needed. Pollis opens when the installation finishes; later, open it from the Start menu. Linux (x64), Pollis-linux-x64.tar.gz: Run tar -xzf Pollis-linux-x64.tar.gz. Run Pollis-linux-x64/pollis. The apps are not signed yet That is why macOS needs the xattr step and Windows may warn you. Download Pollis only from the link above.

If Julia is not installed, the Welcome page says so under Status: Julia is not installed. Choose Install Julia, then Download and Install. Pollis installs it with juliaup, the official Julia version manager, in a terminal. The terminal says when Juliaup and Julia have been installed. The Welcome page's Status then says Julia found, and the Julia REPL starts. If Julia is already installed somewhere Pollis cannot find it, choose Set Julia Path instead, and give the path of the Julia program in the setting julia.executablePath.

section: The first start of the Julia REPL
text: When Pollis opens, the Julia REPL starts in the panel at the bottom. The first time, it installs DuckDB, PollisDatasets and PollisKnowledge, whose texts are downloaded only when switched on in the Knowledge Base, makes the databases of Pollis, the built-in PollisDatasets, PollisJournals, PollisReferences and PollisBenchmarks, and PollisRSS, of its activity, empty until feeds are read (Pollis Databases, page ), and says This happens only once. They go into an environment of Pollis's own, ~/.pollis/julia, which comes after yours: your own versions of these packages are used first. At later starts, PollisDatasets, PollisJournals, PollisReferences, PollisRSS, PollisBenchmarks and PollisKnowledge are updated from GitHub when there is a newer version; offline, the installed copies are kept. Check for Data Package Updates..., in the Pollis menu on macOS and the Help menu on Windows and Linux, looks for a newer version at once and offers to install it, without a restart. The Welcome page announces a newer version, with Update Now and What Changed.

The Powered by: line at the top of a panel names its Julia packages. Beside it, a tick means they are all installed; Install means some are missing, and installs them in the Julia REPL, in your active Julia environment. You do not have to: the code a panel sends to the Julia REPL or to a notebook starts with a line such as Pollis.packages("GLM", "Plots", "PollisDatasets") which installs whichever of them Julia cannot load, and does nothing when all are there. Replications, notebooks and Code Examples begin the same way. The first run of a panel can therefore take a few minutes; the next ones do not.

Pollis asks GitHub once a day for a newer release. When there is one, a badge appears on the Manage gear, and Download Update opens the file for your system in your browser: install it as above. At the first start of a new version, Pollis offers What's New; Help > What's New in Pollis opens the same notes at any time. To stop the checks, set update.mode to none.

Pollis tells you things in four places, each with its own purpose: Status Whether Pollis is ready: Julia and its version, and the databases of Pollis, PollisDatasets, PollisRSS, PollisJournals, PollisReferences and PollisBenchmarks. Always shown; when something is missing it is a warning with its button. Announcements New releases of Julia, DBInterface, PollisDatasets and PollisTeX, until you dismiss them. Shown only when there is one. RSS The newest unread items of the feeds you follow (page ); a camera or a microphone marks a video or a podcast, and a journal's items have the tag of its level and metrics. Its Alerts tab shows your alerts and those that fired (page ). Notifications The bell at the bottom right: what happens while you work, such as new datasets, new content or a toolbox to reload. A faster start If you do not want the Julia REPL at every start, clear julia.startREPLOnStartup. It then starts the first time you send code to it. macOS: ``Pollis is damaged and can't be opened" & Run xattr -cr /Applications/Pollis.app in Terminal, then open Pollis again. Windows: ``Windows protected your PC" & Choose More info, then Run anyway. Julia is not installed, though it is & Choose Set Julia Path and give the path of the Julia program. The first run of a panel seems stuck & Look at the Julia REPL: packages are being installed and compiled. Wait for the prompt to come back. Install stays after installing & The tick appears once Julia has finished; it checks again every few seconds. Not available yet A Mac build for Intel processors, and signed apps.

What a panel is made of, and how to go from its example to code of your own. Research moves back and forth between four activities: exploring, understanding, experimenting and improving, with each sending you back to the others. The menus of Pollis are their technical form: Explore the data and the literature, Model to understand, Simulate to experiment, Optimise to improve. Each item of the Explore, Model, Simulate and Optimise menus opens a panel: a page about one method, with an example you can run as it is, with simulated data or a dataset from PollisDatasets, and then make your own.

The title, and the Powered by: line: the Julia packages the panel uses, each a link to its documentation, with the tick or Install (see Getting Started, page ). Key Points: what the method does and when to use it, in a few lines. Decision Table, in some panels: which variant to use for which data. Illustration, in some panels: a picture of the method or its variants. Example Code: the tabs of the panel's variants (above, Bernoulli, Binomial, …), its inputs, and the code. Changing an input changes the code at once. Next Steps and Learn More, at the bottom (next page). Click a section's name to open or close it.

The buttons below the code send it where you want it: Julia REPL runs it in the Julia REPL, starting it if needed. Send to Notebook opens it in a new Jupyter notebook, with the Julia kernel. Send to Pluto opens it in a new Pluto notebook, in Pollis's browser. Send to Editor opens it in a new, unsaved Julia file, and Copy copies it. Code sent to the Julia REPL or to a notebook starts with the line that installs any missing package.

Choose Edit below the code, and change it: your data, your variables, your options. Choose Save, or Cancel to leave it as it was. A saved example is marked Customised, and the panel shows your version from then on. To go back to the original, choose Restore Default, then Confirm Restore within four seconds. Your version goes to the Trash.

section: Add a tab of your own
text: Choose + at the end of the tabs, type a name and press Enter. The new tab, marked Added, opens empty, for editing: write or paste your code, and Save. To remove it, choose the × on the tab, then Delete; it goes to the Trash. Your examples and tabs are files in ~/.pollis/examples, one folder per panel. They are kept when Pollis is updated.

Visualise, Diagnose, Predict, Compare, Interpret: examples that carry on from the Example Code, using its results. A Next Step runs the Example Code of the tab first when the Julia REPL has not run it yet, or it has changed since, and stops there if the Example Code fails; Send to Editor, Send to Notebook and Send to Pluto put the Example Code before it. Its examples have the same buttons, and can be edited and restored in the same way.

FAQ, when the panel has one: open questions on the method, each with its answer and a link to the wiki that says more. A panel with an FAQ also has closed questions that it does not show, each with 4 to 10 options, the right one among them: they make the Panel FAQ test set of Evaluate Answering Models (page ). Local Wikis: a reference page on the method, in Pollis. Notebook Tutorials: notebooks that work through the method. Multimedia Tutorials: videos and talks. Add / Edit Video adds your own. Explore References: the papers and books behind the method, with Open in Browser and Copy BibTeX to Clipboard. Add / Edit Reference adds your own, from BibTeX, a link or a DOI; they go into your references, in PollisReferences (page ), and Edit corrects a work wherever it is cited. The example data are an example They show how the method works. To use it on your own data, change the lines that load the data, and check that the variables and options still suit your question. An error that a package is not found & Use Julia REPL or Send to Notebook, which install it, or Install on the Powered by: line. The send buttons are greyed out & Finish editing (Save or Cancel); an added tab needs some code first. Not available yet The microphone and speaker buttons beside the title: voice comes in a later version.

The datasets that come with Pollis, your own databases, and the Databases view. Pollis comes with a collection of real datasets, PollisDatasets, that its examples use, and connects to DuckDB, SQLite and PostgreSQL databases. All the work with data is done in Julia: the Databases view shows what is there and writes the code to reach it.

65 real and 2 simulated datasets, such as mroz, airpassengers, iris, and challenger, each with its source and licence. In Julia: datasets() lists them; datasetinfo("mroz") describes one and its columns; data = dataset("mroz") loads one as a Tables.jl table. They are installed the first time the Julia REPL starts (Getting Started, page ). When new datasets are added, a notification says so.

The same datasets are also a DuckDB database, PollisDatasets, one table per dataset, named after it, with a description of the table and of each column. It is read-only, and is rebuilt only when PollisDatasets changes. The Welcome page's Status says when it is ready. Like the other built-in databases (page ), it is a DuckDB file. Open the Databases view, in the secondary side bar on the right (or choose Open Databases View in the notification of new datasets). Click PollisDatasets, marked built-in. It connects in the Julia REPL as pollis. Expand it to see its tables and their columns. Then query it in the Julia REPL with SQL: DBInterface.execute(pollis, "SELECT * FROM mroz WHERE educ > 12")

It has four sections: Pollis Built-In, the databases that come with Pollis; Pollis Activity, those Pollis records as you work; User, your own databases and those shown from the Julia REPL (Pollis Databases, page ); and History, the queries you have run. New, Refresh Schemas, Learn More and New DuckDB Terminal are at the top of the view. Click a connection to connect it in the Julia REPL; Disconnect closes it. A database whose data package Pollis has updated from GitHub shows Updated and the date after its name, with What Changed in its hover, until you open it or for seven days. On a table, Open in Table Viewer shows its rows; right-click it for Preview Rows in Julia REPL. Show Tables and Hide Tables, beside a connection, expand or collapse it; Refresh Schemas, at the top of the view, shows tables you have just created. Right-click a connection for Copy Name, Copy Connection Code, Edit Connection and Delete Connection, which removes only the saved connection, never the database. History lists the queries of the duckdb> and Pollis REPL terminals and of the notebooks' SQL cells, with their rows, how long they took and any error, the newest first; click one to Run Again, Copy SQL or Open in Editor.

SQL should be at hand wherever you are working, without a second database program: all four use the same DuckDB engine, with its full-text search extension, fts, and attach the databases of Pollis, built in and of its activity, read-only. The duckdb> terminal, for SQL alone, without starting Julia: New DuckDB Terminal, at the top of the Databases view (or Databases: New DuckDB Terminal in the Command Palette). It opens an empty database in memory; .help lists its commands, such as .tables, and Ctrl+C stops a long query. ? at the start of an empty line turns the prompt into help?>, as at julia>: the name of a DuckDB function there shows its forms, its description and its examples, as .help name does. DuckDB REPL, in the status bar and in the terminal's + menu, starts it too, and once it runs names its database in its tooltip and offers Show REPL, Restart REPL and Stop REPL. An SQL file (New, then SQL File) runs there: Ctrl+Enter, or Run in DuckDB Terminal in its title bar, runs the selection or the statement at the cursor. A notebook, for queries kept with their results: the SQL cells of a Jupyter notebook (.ipynb), those whose language, at the cell's bottom right, is SQL. Each result is a table, with the type of each column and the number of rows. With DuckDB SQL (Pollis), chosen in the kernel picker, the notebook is SQL alone. Its cells share one database in memory, so a table one cell creates is there for the next; Restart, in the notebook's toolbar, empties it. With the Julia kernel, SQL cells and Julia cells run side by side, on a database of the notebook's own. A statement such as feeds := SELECT * FROM PollisRSS.feeds makes the table feeds and hands it to Julia: in a Julia cell, feeds.title is a column, length(feeds) its number of rows, and sql("SELECT count(*) FROM $feeds") queries it again. With DuckDB SQL (Pollis), CREATE TEMP TABLE feeds AS SELECT ... makes it instead. The Pollis REPL, for a query in the middle of Julia work: Pollis REPL, in the status bar and in the terminal's + menu, opens pollis> in a terminal of its own, beside the Julia REPL and on the same Julia, which it starts if need be; the item is filled while the terminal is open. Type the query, ending in ;; Ctrl+C stops it. Julia code runs there too: what starts with a word of SQL, such as SELECT, FROM or DESCRIBE, or with name :=, is SQL, and anything else is Julia, so describe(df) is Julia and DESCRIBE feeds; SQL. Julia code runs in the Julia REPL, which shows it in full, and its result shows in the terminal too, an error in one line; Ctrl+C stops it too. ?name shows the help of name there, as at julia>. As in an SQL cell, feeds := SELECT ... keeps the result as the table feeds and the Julia variable feeds, a Tables.jl table; instead of drawing it, the terminal gives its rows and columns, and Open in Table Viewer, in blue under them, opens the whole table to browse with one click. In Julia code, sql("SELECT ...") runs a query on the same database, and sql("feeds", "SELECT ...") keeps its result as the table feeds. Drill-down: Pollis REPL, in Help > Documentation > Drill-downs, has worked examples. db = PollisDB.connect(), for Julia code and scripts: a DuckDB connection in memory, shown in the Databases view; PollisDB.connect("sales.duckdb") opens a file instead. A Julia table goes the other way with the macro @share: @share stock_returns = (ticker = ["AAPL"], returns = [0.12]) binds stock_returns, as = would, and copies it into the database of sql, where SQL reads it by its name; @share stock_returns copies it again after a change, and publish(table, "stock_returns") does the same as a function. The Julia REPL's database is Shared Session, under User in the Databases view. While the REPL runs, the duckdb> terminal, the notebooks of DuckDB SQL (Pollis) and the SQL cells of Julia notebooks attach it as SharedSession: SELECT * FROM SharedSession.stock_returns, and .tables lists its tables.

In the Databases view, choose New, then DuckDB, PostgreSQL or SQLite. Give a Connection Name and the Julia Variable that will hold the connection, and choose whether to keep it for all your work (Global) or for this folder only (Current Workspace). For DuckDB or SQLite, choose the database file (Choose File). A DuckDB connection with no file is an empty database in memory: it can read CSV and Parquet files in place, and is lost when you disconnect. Read Only protects a file from changes. For PostgreSQL, give the Host, Port, Database and Username. Check the Generated Code, then Save Connection, or Connect to save it and connect. A connection opened by your own code can be shown in the view as well: con = PollisDB.show(DBInterface.connect(DuckDB.DB, "sales.duckdb"); name = "Sales") PostgreSQL passwords With Ask for Password in the REPL (the default), you type the password in the Julia REPL when you connect: it is never written in the code, in the REPL history or in a file. Without it, the password comes from PGPASSWORD or ~/.pgpass.

Explore > Access Files: the formats by kind, tables (CSV Files, Excel Workbooks), maps, sound and voice, music, and Life Sciences, a submenu for medical imaging, biosignals, genomics and clinical records; the formats not in Pollis yet, such as Parquet, GeoJSON or DICOM, are greyed out, and the toolboxes of a field can bring more. Explore > Access Databases: SQL databases, Pollis's own among them (query, import a CSV, Parquet or JSON file, save a table, export a query). Explore > Access Data Libraries: Hugging Face and Kaggle datasets, Yahoo Finance, Alpha Vantage, US SEC EDGAR, FRED and the European Central Bank. A provider that needs an API key shows Set API key on the Powered by: line; the key is kept in your system's secure storage.

Every PDF opens in the PDF Viewer of Pollis, from the Explorer, File > Open, Help > Documentation, the vignettes, Reports, Article Methods and the sources of Ask Pollis, with its pages, outline, thumbnails, search, zoom and form fields. Explore > PDF Files opens the PDF shown, else the sample of PollisDatasets, for a task: Read (the outline, else the thumbnails), Extract Pages (the pages given, such as 1-3, 7, in one new PDF, or one file per page or per range), Merge Pages, Crop Area (Select Area on) and Convert (that tool open in the sidebar), and the markup tools Highlight, Add or Edit Text, Add or Edit Images and Draw. Every item opens the same viewer, whose toolbar always has Select Area, Print and Save; Open a PDF..., in its title bar, opens a PDF of yours. Tools: Show | Hide, at the right end of the toolbar, shows or hides the sidebar at the right of the pages, with the area of Select Area and the Poppler tools, those that read the PDF and those that make files from it; the viewer keeps the choice for the next PDF. Choose Select Area in the toolbar, and drag a box around a table, a paragraph or a figure. Its frame flashes green, and the sidebar shows its position in points from the top left corner of the page, a picture of it and its table. Copy Text, Copy Table, Save CSV... and Save PNG... take the area away; Text, Table or Image, under Send to Ask Pollis, puts its text, its cells as a CSV file, or a picture of it in the question of the Ask Pollis pane. The Poppler tools, in the sidebar, run Poppler in Julia on the pages given, or on the area with Only the Area: Extract Text (also of the pages given, such as 1-3, 7), Tables, Fonts, Images, Attachments, Document Info, Render Pages, Convert (SVG, PostScript, EPS, HTML or XML, or the area as PDF), Extract Pages (the pages given, such as 1-3, 5, in one file, or a file per page or per range) and Merge Pages. Each tool has its options, Run, and its Julia Code, to copy or run in the REPL. What a tool prints is shown below it; the files it writes go to the folder or the file you choose, and a CSV file shows as a table, a picture as itself and a text file as its text. An attachment chosen in the left pane shows there too. The dialogs open in the folder you chose last, or at first in the PDF's folder, or in Documents for a PDF of a Julia package, as the sample of PollisDatasets; the result names the folder, with Reveal in Finder (Reveal in File Explorer on Windows). Highlight, Add or Edit Text, Add or Edit Images and Draw, in the toolbar, mark up the pages; Save writes the PDF with the marks in a new file. Print, in the toolbar, prints the PDF with the system's print dialog. The internal browser, Explore > Browse the Web, does not show PDFs: a PDF that a page links to opens in the PDF Viewer. It is kept in a temporary folder that is emptied when Pollis quits; File > Save As... keeps a copy. In Ask Pollis, PDF... in the + opens a PDF of yours in the PDF Viewer (Ask Pollis, page ). The view shows no tables & Choose Refresh Schemas. A new database stays empty until you create a table in the Julia REPL. PollisDatasets does not connect & The Julia REPL has not started yet, or is still installing: wait for the Welcome page to say the database is ready. Cannot write to pollis & The built-in database is read-only: save your tables in a database of your own. PostgreSQL does not connect & Check the host, port and SSL Mode; the Connection Timeout is 10 seconds. A Poppler tool says Julia is installing & The first time, Julia installs Poppler, for a minute or two; the tool then runs by itself. For a PDF with a password, give it in Password. Not available yet International Monetary Fund Datasets, World Bank Indicators and the Kenneth French Data Library are in Access Data Libraries, greyed out.

Showing only the menus you need, and making Pollis yours. Pollis has hundreds of panels. A View is a named set of the menu items Pollis shows: a course can keep only its own topics, a researcher only their field. The panels you hide are still there; another View shows them again.

The name of the View in use is in the title bar, before the layout buttons: View: Max. Click it for the Views menu, with a tick on the one in use. Two Views are built in: Max shows every menu item. It is the default. Min shows a short selection: the common plots and Descriptive Statistics in Explore, and a few models, simulations and optimisation panels. Switching applies at once, to every menu. The built-in Views cannot be changed or deleted.

section: Make a View of your own
text: In the Views menu, choose Create View..., type its name, and choose the View it starts from: Max starts with every menu item. Or choose Save View As... to copy the View in use. The new View becomes the one in use, and the Views panel opens in the secondary side bar, on the right, after Databases: the menus, with every item below them. Untick an item to hide it, tick it to show it. Unticking a submenu hides everything in it; a submenu shows how many of its items are shown, such as 4/12. Changes apply at once. Explore, Model, Simulate, Optimise, Extend and Compose can be trimmed to the items you tick; in the other menus, such as File or Help, you can hide single items.

Edit View... makes one of your Views the one in use, and shows its items in the Views panel. Delete View... moves its file to the Trash, so it can be restored. Deleting the View in use switches to Max. Open Views Folder opens ~/.pollis/views: each of your Views is a JSON file there. Copy a file to another computer, or give it to your students, to use the same View. The View in use is kept in the setting pollis.view.

Choose the Manage gear at the bottom left, then Settings, and type in the search box a word or a setting's id, such as julia.startREPLOnStartup. Themes > Color Theme, in the same gear, changes the colours, light or dark.

The Extensions pane, in the activity bar on the left, installs extensions from Open VSX, the open registry of extensions, as well as Pollis toolboxes (next topic). Some extensions published only by Microsoft are not on Open VSX, so they cannot be installed in Pollis.

Your own things are files in ~/.pollis, kept when Pollis is updated: views your Views examples your Example Code and added tabs (Inside a Panel, page ) workflows your copies of the replications (page ) replications the replications you make (page ) methods, packages your new methods and their packages (page ) practice the exercises you write (the Self-Study toolbox) rss the items of your RSS feeds (page ) ask/sets your test sets of Evaluate Answering Models (page ) A hidden item is only hidden A View changes the menus, nothing else: the Command Palette and links between panels still reach every panel. A View is not a way to stop students from opening a panel. A menu item has gone & The View in use hides it: switch to Max, or tick it in your View. The items cannot be ticked & The View in use is built in: choose Save View As... to make an editable copy. An extension is not found & It is not on Open VSX. Look for an open alternative there.

Adding a whole field to Pollis with a toolbox extension. A toolbox is an extension that adds a set of panels to the menus, with their wikis and notebook tutorials. It holds no program code: its panels are made like Pollis's own. A toolbox may cover a field, such as medicine, astrophysics, tourism or music, or a way of working, such as self-study, with Pollis AI+ as a study companion: Self-Study: Learn and Practise, the last below. Lifestyle toolboxes, for everyday tasks such as planning a trip, are coming soon. Four are published: Finance: volatility from daily and intraday prices, high-frequency covariance, ARIMAX, VAR and VECM, GARCH-type and regime switching models, point processes, forecasting, Bayesian asset-pricing factor models. Economics: business cycle filters, stochastic volatility, DSGE and heterogeneous-agent models, continuous-time macro-finance, game theory. Core Mathematics: symbolic maths, linear algebra, nonlinear systems, numerical differentiation and integration, ordinary and partial differential equations. Self-Study: Learn and Practise: turn your slides, notes and PDFs into what helps you study: more problems with their solutions, a topic explained in depth, a summary of a paper, prose and audio from slides, or slides from a long text. For students, and for teachers preparing their classes. Its Self-Study Guide and its vignette are in Help > Documentation > Toolboxes.

Open the Extensions pane, in the activity bar on the left. The Toolboxes section, at the top, lists the toolboxes you have not installed. Click a name for its details. Choose Install. When Pollis asks, choose Reload Now or Restart Extensions. The Toolbox Panels page opens: installing a toolbox does not change your menus until you choose its panels there (next page). An installed toolbox moves to the Installed section. When a newer version is published, it comes back to Toolboxes with Update.

section: Choose its panels, and where they go
text: The Toolbox Panels page shows the toolbox on the left and Your Menus (Preview) on the right. Tick the panels you want (Select All, Select None), or choose Display Author's Suggestion to see where the author would put them. Click a blue line in the preview, Put here, to put the ticked items there. A ticked toolbox menu moves with its panels inside; untick it to move panels out of it. Choose Publish. The page then says In your menus as shown. A toolbox can go in Explore, Model, Simulate, Optimise or their submenus, or in Extend, a menu that appears only when a toolbox puts something in it. To change them later, choose Edit on the toolbox in the Installed section, or Toolbox Panels... in the Command Palette (Compose: Toolbox Panels...). To remove a toolbox, choose Uninstall on it in the same section. A toolbox can bring its own vignette, a brief overview of what its menu items and panels are for: Help > Documentation > Toolbox Vignettes lists those of the toolboxes you installed, and Pollis compiles one the first time you open it. A toolbox can also bring notebook courses of its field to Help > Notebook Courses: the Finance Toolbox brings Financial Risk Forecasting, and the Economics Toolbox the QuantEcon Julia Lectures.

A teacher can package the panels of a course as one toolbox and give it to the students. This is done by your coding agent (Orchestration, page ), with a skill that writes the toolbox for you. Choose Compose > Package a Toolbox... The agent starts in a terminal. Tell it which panels you want, by their menu titles, the menus they go in and their order, and the toolbox's name and description. It asks for what is missing. It writes a short spec, builds the toolbox and its README, and says where the .vsix file is. Each toolbox has a folder of its own, in the toolboxes folder of your Pollis Workspace (Reports, page , says how to make one), with its spec, toolbox.toml, its README and its .vsix files, in dist. To install it, run Extensions: Install from VSIX... in the Command Palette and choose the file. Your students do the same with the file you give them. Then choose its panels, as on the previous page. To change it, edit the spec, raise its version, build again and install the new file over the old one.

Compose > New Panels > Create a Panel... has your coding agent write a new panel with you. Create Panels from a Request... writes several at once from a request file, which lists the toolbox and, for each panel, its topic, methods and menu. Without a request file open, it opens an example to fill in. The new panels go in the panels folder of your Pollis Workspace, and can then be packaged as a toolbox. Toolboxes need the Internet to install The list of toolboxes and their files come from GitHub. Once installed, a toolbox works offline. ``Could not load the list of toolboxes" & Check the Internet connection, then choose Retry. Installed, but nothing in the menus & Choose its panels and Publish: Edit on the toolbox, in Installed. The Toolbox Panels page is empty & Reload the window or restart the extensions, as Pollis asked, first. A panel cannot go in a toolbox & Some Pollis panels have code of their own and are marked not portable; the agent says which. Replication, Methods and Workflows Replay a classic. Keep what it teaches. Besides its replication record, a replicated article can leave two things behind: a new method, and a workflow.

It starts from an article, its input data, and either the results it publishes or its authors' code, in any language. Each published table is computed by Julia packages, by notebook code or by a new method. Then each result is printed beside the published one. Replication, page .

A method an article needed and no Julia package had becomes a documented Julia package. Its tests run the article's data and check the published results, within tolerances. It comes with a vignette, and can be published in the Pollis registry. Article Methods, page .

A flat set of procedures, each with its inputs, its outputs and what it runs. Extracted from a replication, it runs on your own data; combined with others, its independent procedures run side by side. Not available yet Extract a Workflow..., in a replication's last step, and Browse Workflows..., Extract a Workflow... and Combine Workflows... in Compose > Workflows.

Replaying a classic paper from its own data, step by step. A replication reproduces a published analysis on its own public data: a Jupyter notebook that follows the article section by section and prints every published value beside Julia's. It shows a method at work on a real question, and that Julia gets the published answer. Pollis comes with ten, below; Replicate an Article makes your own.

Replication Article Panel data: is public capital productive? Munnell (1990) GARCH: volatility after non-trading days Bollerslev and Ghysels (1996) Survival: the Mayo model for primary biliary cirrhosis Dickson et al. (1989) Logistic regression: the Challenger O-rings Dalal, Fowlkes and Hoadley (1989) Threshold autoregression: the lynx and the sunspot cycles Tong and Lim (1980) Dynamic time warping: the UCR archive baselines Dau et al. (2019) Propensity score matching: the NSW experiment and its replications Dehejia and Wahba (1999) Random forests: Breiman (2001) Breiman (2001) LSTNet: long- and short-term patterns in multivariate time series Lai, Chang, Yang and Liu (2018) Long-run risks: the model and aggregate asset prices Beeler and Campbell (2012)[1]

Choose Compose > Article Replication > Browse Replications... The page lists yours first, In Progress and Done by You: click a title to open its page. The Library follows, with each replication's article (its DOI, or Web Page when it has none, and Copy BibTeX), the Julia packages and datasets it uses, its size, any data it downloads, and the date it was last updated. Click more under a description to read it all. Click a name in the Library. The first time, Pollis makes your own copy in ~/.pollis/workflows, and opens its notebook. Your copy is yours to change: later openings show it as you left it. Delete and Delete Empty Replications move folders of yours to the Trash.

Choose the Julia kernel if the notebook asks for one. Run the cells in order, from the top. The first code cell, Pollis.packages(...), installs any package that is missing, so the first run takes longer. Read each section beside the article: the text says which table, figure or page it replicates. The data come from PollisDatasets or from the source the article used. The page says when a replication downloads data, and how much (+ size download); download if asked marks data that it downloads only when you agree.

Most comparisons are small tables: Julia's value in full, the same value rounded as the article prints it, the published value, and the number of decimals they share, or DIFFERENT. Each table's title says where the published value is printed, usually a page or table. Random forests averages 100 random runs, as Breiman did, so it asks instead whether Julia's average and Breiman's differ by less than two standard errors, beyond the rounding of the printed value. All the notebooks but the panel-data one end with a section, What differs, and why.

New replications, and new versions of the ones you have, can arrive between releases of Pollis: the page marks them New or Updated until you open them. When your copy is older than the new version, the page says Your copy is older than this version and offers Open Updated Version: the new notebook is saved beside yours, with its date in the name, and your copy is kept. From a replication to a report A replication's notebook can become a LaTeX report or slides: Reports, page . The GARCH replication has its own report template.

Compose > Article Replication > Replicate an Article... opens a page of five numbered steps; click its title to change it. Nothing is saved until you type or add something. Each replication is a folder in ~/.pollis/replications. Article and Data: the Article Link, the Input Tables and the Target Tables, as for a method (Article Methods, page ). Each input has a licence, the terms its provider states, and the page warns of each input with none stated. Plan, optional: for each target, Computed By is Julia Packages, Notebook Code or Article Method, with a Note, saved as you change it. Values is Exact, compared to the digits printed, or Random, as for a simulation, the bootstrap or a random forest, compared within its Monte Carlo noise from the Runs in Julia and the Runs in the Article. Choose in each row, or have Ask Agent propose a plan. Make an Article Method, on a table's row, starts a method for that table, and the notebook can hold its code until the method is written. Replicate: write Instructions, saved in INSTRUCTIONS.md, and click Replicate with Agent. Your coding agent writes the notebook and runs it, and Pollis.replicate and Pollis.compare write each comparison to results.csv. Open Notebook opens it. Compare: the precision each table requires, Decimals Required or, for random values, Standard Errors Allowed, and the values short of it (Show every value for all). Give each a Kind, Misprint, Rounding, Not Replicable or Unexplained, and an Explanation, saved as you type; Explain with Agent proposes them. Record and Share: how many tables and values are at the precision they require, and how many differences are explained. Add to My Replications lists it under Done by You. Add from Article and the three with Agent buttons run your coding agent, on your account. A cell fails: a package is not found & Run the first code cell, Pollis.packages(...), then the others in order. A download fails & Check the Internet connection; the source may be down for a while. Try again later. You changed your copy and want the original & Rename or delete its folder in ~/.pollis/workflows; opening the replication again makes a fresh copy. Not available yet Browse Workflows..., Extract a Workflow..., Combine Workflows..., Create Operational Workflow... and Automations..., in Compose > Workflows, are in the menu but not built yet, nor is Extract a Workflow... in a replication's Record and Share.

Turning a new method into a tested Julia package, with its vignette. A new method is one no Julia package has yet, taken from an article: its data, the results the article publishes for them, and the code that reproduces them. Pollis makes it a Julia package whose tests are the published values, with a vignette, its documentation, and can publish it in the Pollis registry. Without data and expected results there is no new method.

Compose > Article Replication > Create Article Method... opens the method's page, with five numbered steps, below; its title is at the top: click it to change it. Nothing is saved until you type or add something. Each method is a folder in ~/.pollis/methods.

Article: the Article Link. Pollis opens it in the integrated browser, and a PDF in the PDF Viewer, and keeps no copy; Save a Copy... saves one outside Pollis, by default in the data folder of your Pollis Workspace (Reports, page ). Input Tables, the data the method is computed from: Empty Table to type one in, Add from a Link, Add from PollisDatasets, or Add from Article: give the numbers of the article's tables, such as 3.2, 5.8, and click Ask Agent. Target Tables, the published results the method must reproduce: Empty Table, Add from CSV Files, or Add from Article. Every printed value becomes a test of the package. A table typed in by the agent keeps every value as printed, and the agent lists the values it could not read for certain: check them against the article. The tests are only as right as the targets.

Write Instructions for the agent, saved in INSTRUCTIONS.md: what the method does, where it is in the article, what to watch for. Then click Write Method: your coding agent writes the code in src, with you, and runs the tests. Edit method.toml shows the method's own file: its tables, its call and its article. Open Code opens the code.
Once the method's tests pass, write notes on the vignette (VIGNETTE.md) and click Write Vignette: the agent writes it in LaTeX, with its PDF. Edit Vignette and Open PDF open them.

Give the Package Name: a capital letter, then letters and digits, such as ThresholdAR; the Pollis registry asks for at least 5 characters. It also asks for a usage example and a docstring for every exported name: Prepare for Registration has the agent check the method and fix what it can.

Each button runs in a terminal. Package and Test makes the package in ~/.pollis/packages, runs its tests and checks the registry rules. Package, Test and Push to GitHub then pushes it to its own public repository, if its tests all pass. Package, Test, Push and Register then registers it, if it meets the rules. Pushing needs a GitHub Owner, a user or organization, and the GitHub CLI, gh, signed in; Pollis asks first: Push to GitHub as …?

Compose > Article Replication > Browse Article Methods... lists yours In Progress, then the Library of the published methods, those by Pollis, from arc-fs to two-scales realized volatility, and those you pushed with Package and Publish, each with its Author: click a heading to sort by it, and a method to open your own copy. Delete and Delete Empty Article Methods move folders to the Trash. Help > Documentation > Package Vignettes lists, in one table, the vignettes of the packages in the registry and of those on your computer, marked Installed (they open offline); click a heading to sort by it. The agent steps cost tokens Add from Article, Write Method, Write Vignette and Prepare for Registration run your coding agent, on your account. …has no target tables, so nothing to test & Add the published results in Target Tables. Copies are kept outside Pollis & Save the copy outside ~/.pollis, e.g. in a Pollis Workspace. The push fails & Sign in with gh auth login in a terminal, and check the GitHub Owner.

Your own forecasting method, scored on a published competition and placed among its entries. A forecasting competition gives many forecasters the same series without their future values, then scores every forecast on what happened. The page runs a method of yours on the series of a competition, scores it with that competition's own measures, as its organisers scored the entries, and shows where it would have finished. It holds five of the M competitions, from the package PollisCompetitions, which Pollis installs from the Pollis registry (Pollis Packages, page ). Competition Series Measures, and the entries M1 (1982) ,001 yearly, quarterly and monthly sMAPE, MASE and OWA, beside Naive2 M3 (2000) ,003 yearly, quarterly, monthly and other sMAPE, MASE and OWA, beside Naive2 M4 (2018) ,000 of six frequencies sMAPE, MASE and OWA; ranked among 61 entries M5 Accuracy (2020) ,490 daily sales of products in stores WRMSSE; ranked among 74 entries M6 (2022) assets, 12 rounds of 4 weeks RPS, IR and OR; ranked among its teams

Pick a competition. Download fetches one that is not on this computer, in the Julia REPL, and checks every file against the digest in PollisCompetitions' catalogue. Then choose the Frequency, and the Series to Run: All, or A Sample of a number of series drawn with a Seed. The same seed draws the same series, so two methods can be compared on one sample. M5 and M6 always run whole.

Write a Julia function forecast(y, h, period): the values the forecasters saw, the number of steps to forecast and the seasonal period, 1 for none; it returns h forecasts. The example is the benchmark Theta of M4. For M6 the function is decide(prices, date): at each round, the prices of the 100 assets up to its first day; it returns, for each asset, the probabilities that its return ranks in each fifth, and the weight invested in it. Its example is M6 Dummy. Reset to the Example brings the example back; any package installed in your Julia session can be loaded with using.

Run the Method writes a folder for the run in ~/.pollis/competitions/runs, with method.jl and run.jl, and runs it in the Julia REPL. The series are forecast over the threads of the session: start Julia with --threads=auto for more at a time. The step shows how many are done; method.jl, run.jl and forecasts.csv open the run's files. Earlier runs... reopens a run, and New Run starts another.

Scores gives the method's scores beside the benchmarks, published or computed on the same series. Place ranks the method among the entries' published scores, when the run is on the series they were scored on: all of M4 or one of its frequencies, all of M5, or the 12 rounds of M6. A Series plots a series with the method's forecast and, when its forecasts are on this computer, the winner's; for M6, By Round gives the scores of each round beside M6 Dummy's.

Errors by Horizon, the errors at each step ahead; Browse the Series, one series at a time; Where It Fails, the series where the method does worst against Naive2; Compare With an Entry, an entry of M4 or M5 on the run's series; Compare Two Runs, two runs on the same series, side by side. Learn More has the wikis: the competitions, the error measures, scoring a method, and the licences and sizes of the downloads. The downloads are large M4 is about 275 MB, M5 about 365 MB. The forecasts of an entry are fetched only when asked for, by Compare in Compare With an Entry, or with download_forecasts of PollisCompetitions. …is not on this computer yet & Click Download in step 1, and wait for the Julia REPL to finish. Your method must define a function … & Name the function forecast, or decide for M6. The run stops on a series & Score and Rank names the first series that failed, with its error: fix method.jl and run again. No place among the entries & A sample, and M1 and M3, are scored but not ranked.

The Julia packages written for Pollis, which you can also use without it. Most panels use Julia packages from Julia's General registry. This topic describes sixteen packages of Pollis's own: ten methods, and six more behind panels and features. All are public on GitHub, under Trumpingtons, with the MIT licence, and work in any Julia session, with or without Pollis. None is in the General registry.

The ten methods of the Library in Compose > Article Replication > Browse Article Methods... (Article Methods, page ). Each is tested against the published results of the article it comes from, has a vignette, and is in the Pollis registry. Package Topic Tested against ArcFS Boosting Breiman's arc-fs, from his random forests article BreslowCox Survival analysis The Mayo model of primary biliary cirrhosis ErrorComponents Panel econometrics Baltagi's tables for the Grunfeld, gasoline and public capital data ForestOOB Random forests Breiman's out-of-bag errors and variable importance GLMExtras GLM inference Dalal, Fowlkes and Hoadley's Challenger O-ring analysis LSTNet Time series forecasting Lai, Chang, Yang and Liu's LSTNet-Skip and their PyTorch code PeriodicGARCH Volatility Bollerslev and Ghysels's periodic GARCH PropensityMatching K-nearest neighbours Dehejia and Wahba, and its replications ThresholdAR Nonlinear dynamics Tong and Lim's threshold autoregression TwoScalesVolatility High-frequency volatility Zhang, Mykland and Aı̈t-Sahalia's two-scales estimator on the Heston model

Add the Pollis registry once, then add packages by name, in the Julia REPL's package mode (type ]): pkg> registry add https://github.com/Trumpingtons/PollisRegistry pkg> add ThresholdAR Help > Documentation > Package Vignettes opens the vignettes of the packages in the registry, those you installed marked Installed.

Package What it does Where Pollis uses it PollisDatasets small, well-known datasets for examples and teaching, as Tables.jl column tables The built-in database (Data and Databases, page ), Add from PollisDatasets in Article Methods, and the examples of panels and replications PollisTeX Typesets LaTeX from Julia with Tectonic, downloaded on first use Compose > Reports (Reports, page ) EDGAR Fetches SEC EDGAR filings and financial data Explore > Access Data Libraries > US SEC EDGAR HARE Heteroskedasticity and autocorrelation estimators Model > Linear Models: Linear Models with Heteroskedasticity, with Autocorrelation and with Heteroskedasticity + AR(1) PollisCompetitions The M forecasting competitions, M1 to M6: their series, entries and published scores, their own measures, and the benchmarks of M4 Compose > Forecasting Competitions (Forecasting Competitions, page ) EventStudies Event studies: intraday studies of SEC filings and of FOMC releases, and panel event studies Model > Event Studies

Pollis installs these packages by itself when a panel, a replication or a report needs them. All six are in the Pollis registry: to install one yourself, add it by name, as the method packages: pkg> add HARE The datasets' own terms The MIT licence covers PollisDatasets' code. Each dataset keeps the terms of its provider: datasetinfo("penguins") shows its description, the source to cite, its licence and its columns. add ThresholdAR: the package is not found & Add the Pollis registry first, as above.

From a notebook to a LaTeX report or slides. Any Jupyter notebook, a replication's or your own, can become a LaTeX report (an article) or beamer slides, with its outputs and figures and a PDF beside it. Pollis does this in its Julia REPL, without an agent; a coding agent can then polish the draft into a finished document.

section: Before you start: a Pollis Workspace
text: Reports are written in the reports folder of a Pollis Workspace: an ordinary folder for your own work, outside Pollis. To make one, choose File > New Pollis Workspace..., give the folder a name (it starts as Pollis Workspace, in your Documents), and click Create. Pollis makes the folder, puts a pollis.toml file in it and a folder for each kind of file, each with a README: data (your datasets and saved copies), knowledge_base (your books, articles and reports, and your references), reports, methods, workflows, panels, toolboxes (the toolboxes you make to share your panels), programs (the programs and libraries compiled in Compilation Lab) and changes, and opens it. Pollis looks in these folders first; pollis.toml names them, so a folder you rename is renamed there too. Next time, choose File > Open Pollis Workspace..., or File > Open Recent. Opened with it, a folder that is not a Pollis Workspace yet becomes one if you agree, keeping what it has.

Open the notebook, for example your copy of a replication (page ). Choose Compose > Reports > Export Notebook as LaTeX... for a report, or Make Slides from a Notebook... for slides. The notebook's own toolbar has the same two in its Export button: LaTeX Report... and Beamer Slides.... With no notebook open, Pollis asks you to choose one, starting in ~/.pollis/workflows. The Julia REPL installs PollisTeX if it is missing, runs the notebook's code cells in order and compiles the document. The .tex opens in the editor, and the PDF beside it, in the PDF Viewer. The files are in reports/NAME of the workspace, NAME being the notebook's: report.tex or slides.tex and its PDF, each cell's printed output in outputs/cellN.txt, and its figure in figures/cellN.pdf.

A report is a draft of the notebook's text cells, with the printed outputs and figures in their place and without the code. Slides have a frame for the text under each heading, and one for each output and each figure. A notebook with a template, a latex folder beside it, gets that document instead, with its own tables, figures and references. The GARCH replication ships one for its report.

Edit the .tex as you like, then click Compile LaTeX, the play button at the top right of its editor: Pollis saves it, compiles it with PollisTeX in the Julia REPL and reloads the PDF. Exporting the notebook again refreshes the outputs and figures, and keeps your .tex: Pollis writes it only when the folder has none. To start the draft again, delete the .tex first.

Open the report's or the slides' .tex. Choose Compose > Reports > Polish with Agent... The coding agent starts in a terminal in the report's folder. It turns the draft into a finished document: sections, tables, captions and citations, from the numbers already computed. It does not run the notebook again, and it compiles the document as it goes: the PDF beside you reloads each time. Polish runs on the Light tier of Model Tasks and Routing (Orchestration, page ). Polish costs tokens The menu item with the sparkle runs your coding agent, on your account. Read the result: an agent can still misplace a value, so check the numbers against the draft. Reports are written in the reports folder of a Pollis Workspace & Click New Pollis Workspace..., or open your workspace folder. A Pollis Workspace keeps your work outside Pollis & Choose a folder outside ~/.pollis, for example in your Documents. No PDF appears & A cell or the compile failed: read the error in the Julia REPL, fix it, and export or compile again. Polish says to open the .tex & Open report.tex or slides.tex first, then choose Polish with Agent... again.

Following news, journals, central banks, searches, podcasts and videos, and keeping what they bring. Explore > RSS > RSS Feeds opens a page with the feeds you follow on the left, by topic, and their items on the right. Pollis reads every feed when it starts and then every hour; Refresh reads them at once. The feeds are read by your computer, not by a server of Pollis. At first, Pollis follows only the Julia news; a notification at the first launch points to the catalogue, where you choose the rest. Every feed is RSS to Pollis, wherever it comes from: most come from the catalogue, about 520 feeds in 35 categories, from PollisRSS.jl and updated without a new Pollis, ranging from Classics and Philosophy to Economics and Astronomy, all listed on the page in alphabetical order; some are searches you save, at arXiv or PubMed; and some are email alerts, saved searches whose results arrive by email, which Pollis turns into feeds. They are read, shown, archived and added to Zotero alike.

Explore > RSS > Add Feed..., or Add Feed on the RSS Feeds page, opens a page with these sections: From an Address a feed's address, the page of a journal or a website, or a YouTube channel or its @handle; Find From a Search a PubMed or arXiv search, such as abs:"survival analysis" AND cat:stat.ME; Preview first From Email Alerts the alerts mailbox, and the alerts that arrived in it, ticked to follow (below) Your Feeds the feeds you added, with Remove; under Removed Feeds, Restore For a journal's page at Wiley, Taylor & Francis, SAGE, Elsevier, Cambridge Core or Oxford Academic, Find gets the feed of its newest issues; for another website, the feeds its page lists, to choose from when there are several. Then pick the topic to list the feed under, or New Topic....

Click a topic or a feed on the left to see its items, or All Feeds. The feeds of a topic are indented under it, with a camera after the name of a feed of videos and a microphone after a podcast's. Every topic of the catalogue is listed; one with no feed subscribed starts collapsed. The last column, Unread / Total, counts the items of the Items From period. The items are shown 100 at a time, newest first; Previous and Next, above and under them, turn the pages. Click an item to open it in your browser; it is then marked read, and its title is no longer bold. Mark Unread, shown when the pointer is on a read item, marks it unread again. An item of a podcast or a video has a Listen or Watch link; Pollis tells them by the feed, or by the item's address (a news site's video or audio page). Three columns of circles, for a feed or for all the feeds of a topic: green when on, red when off, half green and half red when only some of a topic's feeds are on; the last two are under Display. Subscribed: Pollis reads the feed every hour, and a catalogue feed ticked is followed (its count is a dash until then); unticked, it is no longer read, but its items stay. Here: its items are shown on this page; unticked, they are hidden here and on the welcome page, but the feed is still read and archived, and the right says No items shown when every item of a choice is hidden. Welcome Page: its newest unread items are in the welcome page's RSS section. Items From sets how far back items are shown: The Last 7 Days, 30 (the default), 90, or All Items Kept. Items without a date are always shown. On a Day... shows the items of one day, chosen in a calendar. Only the latest items of each feed are kept here, and the archive goes back only to the day you started following it: a feed cannot tell what happened before then. An item of a journal has a purple tag: the journal's level in the Norwegian register (Level 2 leading, Level 1 academic, Level 0 not academic), OpenAlex's 2-year mean citedness (Cited 7.9), and, once you have imported them (Pollis Databases, page ), the SJR or Impact Factor quartile and its year (SJR Q1 2025). The pointer on the tag shows every value known, with its source and year: SJR and its categories, SNIP, IPP, h-index, open access. Pollis knows the journal of a catalogue feed, of an email alert's article, and of a feed you added, by looking up its first items once. Journals, next to Items From, shows only the items of some journals: Academic (Level 1 or 2), Leading (Level 2), Open Access, and, once imported, SJR Q1, SJR Q1–Q2 and SNIP Above 1. Items not from a journal (news, blogs, preprints) always stay, and the counts follow the choice. Remove, shown when the pointer is on a feed, takes it off the page; Restore, under Removed Feeds on the Add Feed page, brings it back.

Explore > RSS > Journal Metrics, More Metrics... in Journals, the i next to it, or a click on a tag opens the Journal Metrics page: each source's metrics, their values and meaning, and more to import (page ).

Add to Zotero, shown when the pointer is on an item, adds it to Zotero 7 or later, open on the same computer: an article from PubMed as a journal article, an arXiv, medRxiv or bioRxiv paper as a preprint, a video or a podcast episode as such, and anything else as a web page. When Zotero has collections, Pollis asks which one, starting from the last one you chose. The item then shows In Zotero, and is listed in the zotero view of PollisRSS (below), with the collection. For an open-access paper, an arXiv, bioRxiv or medRxiv preprint or a PLOS article, Zotero also downloads its PDF and attaches it. For any other article, use Zotero's own Find Available PDF (right-click the item in Zotero), which finds a free copy when there is one. Export as OPML saves the feeds you follow as one file, to follow them in Zotero (File > New Feed > From OPML...) or another feed reader. PubMed searches and email alerts are left out, since only Pollis reads them.

Every item Pollis reads is added to a monthly file in ~/.pollis/rss/items, so an item stays when its feed drops it. PollisRSS is a DuckDB database over those files, made with PollisDatasets the first time the Julia REPL starts (Data and Databases, page ), and empty until feeds are read: In the Databases view, click PollisRSS, under Pollis Activity. It connects in the Julia REPL as rss, read-only. Query its four views: items, one row per item (feed, topic, title, link, published, received, summary, picture and media); feeds, one row per feed with its number of items; zotero, the items added to Zotero; and episodes, the podcast episodes downloaded. DBInterface.execute(rss, "SELECT topic, count(*) FROM items GROUP BY topic")

An item of a podcast has Download Episode, which saves its audio file in ~/.pollis/rss/episodes, a folder per podcast; the notification's Open Folder shows it, and the item then shows Downloaded. The episode is listed in the episodes view of PollisRSS, with the file. Videos are not downloaded, since YouTube's terms do not allow it, and news pages stay links.

Google Scholar, JSTOR, HeinOnline, Nexis Uni, SSRN, Semantic Scholar, Web of Science, Scopus, Westlaw and Factiva send the results of a saved search only by email. Send them to an address of your own, best one used only for alerts, and Pollis turns each alert into a feed, with the title, the link, and the authors and journal of each result. Pollis reads the mailbox on your computer over IMAP, read only: nothing passes through a server. Add Feed, From Email Alerts: the address, its IMAP server (suggested for Gmail, iCloud, Yahoo, Fastmail and GMX) and its password, kept in the system's keychain; then Connect. Gmail, iCloud and Yahoo need an app password; Outlook.com does not let programs in with a password. Create the alerts at each source, sent to that address. The Email Alerts skill, in Compose > Agent Skills, walks you through each source and writes precise searches in its syntax, so the alerts bring few false hits. Alerts in the Mailbox lists the alerts that have arrived, by source; the ones you tick are listed under the topic Email Alerts. Google Alerts (Show options > Deliver to > RSS feed) and the table-of-contents alerts of many publishers are feeds already: paste their address in From an Address; Search Feeds from Other Services there shows where EBSCOhost and ProQuest give theirs. Alerts on quotes, SEC filings and economic data Warnings when a quote crosses a level, a company files at the SEC or a series publishes a new value are not feeds: Alerts, page . Press releases from PR Newswire, and what the news said around an event: Media Coverage, page . Could not be read the last time; the items shown are the ones read before & The feed's site did not answer, or moved: try Refresh later, or remove the feed and add its new address. No feed found at this address & On the journal's page, look for an RSS link and copy its address; for an Oxford journal, the RSS icon on its page. The mailbox could not be read & Check the address, the server and the password; Gmail, iCloud and Yahoo need an app password, and IMAP turned on. Zotero is not open & Open Zotero 7 or later on this computer, and click Add to Zotero again. The episode could not be downloaded & The podcast's site did not answer: check the internet connection and click Download Episode again. A YouTube channel shows no videos & YouTube's feeds are sometimes unavailable for a while: the items come at a later reading.

What the news said about a company, an institution or a subject, and when. Explore > Media Coverage counts the articles about a company, an institution or a subject over a period, by hour, day or week, marks the FOMC's releases, a company's SEC filings or a time of your own on the same chart, and lists the articles, newest first. Pollis shows the headlines and links only; an article opens in the internal browser.

Words: what the articles must have. Quotes keep a phrase together ("Apple Inc"); OR between words takes any of them, in parentheses: (iPhone OR iPad). Words can be a subject, such as "going concern", or an institution: "FOMC" OR "Federal Reserve". Sources: tick the ones to search; Pollis keeps your choice. Yahoo Finance has a Ticker box beside it (AAPL): its headlines, and the company's SEC filings for Mark. Period: Last 24 Hours, Last 3 Days, Last 7 Days, Last 30 Days, Last 90 Days, Last Year, or From a Day to a Day, with a From and a To day of your own. Mark: Nothing, FOMC Releases, SEC Filings of the Ticker or A Time, of your own; then Search.

Google News papers and sites the world over, among them those with no search of their own, such as The Washington Post and The Times; at most 100 articles a search Yahoo Finance the latest headlines of the ticker: the newest only, not the whole period The New York Times its Article Search, with your own free key: the newest 50 articles of the period The Guardian its Open Platform, with your own free key: the newest 1,000 articles of the period PR Newswire companies' and organisations' own press releases; unticked at first

section: The keys of The New York Times and The Guardian
text: Both give a free key for personal use. Beside each, Get a Free Key opens its sign-up page in the internal browser; Set Key... asks for the key, kept in the system's keychain, never in a file. Change Key... replaces it; left empty, the key is forgotten. A source ticked without a key says No key set and is skipped; the others are still searched.

Coverage gives the number of articles from each source, listed of those it found, and a chart of them by hour, for up to 3 days, by day, for up to half a year, or by week. A mark is a dashed line where it falls. Click a bar to list only its articles, and Show the Whole Period to list them all again. Articles lists each with When, From (the outlet), Headline and Source. The same story told twice, by an outlet and its copy elsewhere, is listed once.

A paid distribution service: companies and organisations pay it to put out their own press releases, unedited. Most are corporate (results, deals, dividends, products), but they come from every sector, from health to technology to entertainment, often before the 8-K that EDGAR shows, and with their time to the second. Its feeds list only the latest releases, so Pollis reads them every 10 minutes while PR Newswire is ticked here, or while there is an event study of SEC filings, and keeps them on this computer. A search finds only the releases out since then: those that have all its words, or give the ticker as the wires do, such as (NASDAQ: AAPL). From an event study Each event of an event study has a News link (Event Studies, page ): it opens Media Coverage from the day before the event to the day after, with the event marked. For an FOMC release, the words are "FOMC" OR "Federal Reserve"; for a filing, the company's name, with its ticker. The other wires GlobeNewswire and Business Wire keep programs away from their feeds, and Pollis respects that: their releases, and ACCESS Newswire's, come through Google News, with the time it gives, which can be later than the release. What it does not do Google News lists at most about 100 articles a search: over a long period, or for a company much in the news, it leaves gaps, and a shorter period, or more precise Words, finds more. FOMC releases go back about a year, as far as the Federal Reserve's feed. Pollis counts articles; it does not read them or judge their tone. No key set: The New York Times & Get a Free Key, then Set Key... beside it, or untick it. Not reached: Google News & Check the internet connection and Search again; the articles of the other sources are still shown. Nothing found & Fewer or broader words, without quotes, or a longer period. Search stays grey & Tick a source, and give Words or a Ticker, and a whole period. No PR Newswire releases & Only the releases out since it was ticked are kept: search a later period.

Being told when a quote or an economic series does something unusual, or when a company files something new at the SEC. An alert watches one thing for you while Pollis is open: a quote at Yahoo Finance, looked up every minute; a company's filings at the SEC's EDGAR, looked at every 15 minutes; or an economic series at FRED, the ECB, the IMF or the World Bank, looked up every hour. When it fires, a notification stays until you act on it, in the colour you chose, and the status bar shows how many fired alerts you have not read. Nothing runs on a server: when Pollis is closed, nothing is watched.

Explore > Alerts > Add Alert..., with Alert On set to A Quote. Symbol: an index (^GSPC), a share (AAPL), a future (BZ=F) or a currency (EURUSD=X); Look Up shows its latest value and a chart over 1 Day, 5 Days, 1 Month or 6 Months. Alert Me When It: Crosses Above or Crosses Below a value; Is Above or Is Below it, once until it is back on the other side; or Moves By more than a percentage since the previous close. The value is drawn across the chart. Or one of the statistical conditions below. Shows As Information, Warning or Error; Fires Every Time the condition is met anew, or Once, after which the alert is paused. Then Add Alert. The quotes are delayed by up to about 20 minutes, depending on the exchange.

Add Alert..., with Alert On set to Economic Data, and From: FRED, ECB, IMF or World Bank. FRED asks for a free API key, set once with Set FRED Key and shared with the FRED panel. Series: a FRED series ID (CPIAUCSL, UNRATE); an ECB dataset and key (EXR/D.USD.EUR.SP00.A); an IMF dataflow and key; or a country and a World Bank indicator (PRT/NY.GDP.PCAP.KD). Look Up shows its title, latest value and period, frequency, units and a chart. Alert Me When It Publishes a New Value; crosses, or is above or below, a value; Changes By at least an amount from the value before; or a statistical condition. The first look only notes the latest period; from then on, each new period is checked. A revision of a period already published does not fire. Open Series opens the series at its source.

For a quote or a series, an alert can fire on what is unusual for it, rather than on a value you choose. OnlineStats.jl computes these in Julia, in a hidden process that Pollis starts when needed; the first time, it installs OnlineStats and JSON3 in an environment of its own, ~/.pollis/alerts/julia, which takes about half a minute. Your own environments are not touched. A quote's move is from one minute to the next, as a log return; a series' move is its change from the value before. Moves Unusually: a move larger than so many Standard Deviations of the moves before it. Leaves Its Band: the value leaves the band of so many standard deviations around its mean; once, until it is back within. Moves Beyond a Quantile: a move beyond that quantile, in per cent, of the moves before it; above 50 a rise, below 50 a fall. Makes a New High or Low: above the highest or below the lowest of so many Values Before It. The mean and the standard deviation weigh recent values more: Half-Life, in Values is after how many a value weighs half as much. The chart then shows what the alert would have done: its band over each minute of the last five days' regular sessions, or over the series' latest values, with a dot where it would have fired, and how many times. Change the numbers until it fires as rarely as you want. Open Notebook beside the count opens alert.ipynb, which computes the same with OnlineStats.jl over the same values, to check it or try other settings; your changes to it are kept.

EDGAR is where companies listed in the United States publish their reports: the annual 10-K, the quarterly 10-Q, and the 8-K for events that cannot wait, such as results, a merger or a new chief executive. Explore > Alerts > Add Alert..., with Alert On set to SEC Filings. The first time, Set Contact: your name and email, which the SEC asks for with every request. It is kept in your system's keychain and shared with the US SEC EDGAR panel; it is sent only to the SEC. For: One Company, Several Companies, An Industry or Every Company, the last only with Contains, as there are thousands of filings a day. Company: a ticker (AAPL) or the SEC's CIK (320193); Look Up lists its recent filings, those of the chosen forms and items in bold. Companies: tickers or CIKs separated by commas. Industry: an SIC code, such as 2834 for pharmaceuticals (SIC Codes opens the SEC's list); every company the SEC files under it, listed or not. Forms: separated by commas, 10-K, 10-Q, 8-K at first. An amendment (10-K/A) counts as its form; left empty, every filing fires. 8-K Items, when the forms take in 8-Ks: an 8-K then fires only when it reports one of the items ticked, such as 2.02 Results of Operations, 5.02 Directors or Officers Changed or 4.02, a restatement; none ticked, every 8-K fires. Contains, optional: words the filing must have, in EDGAR's full-text search; an exact phrase in quotes, such as "going concern". Search lists the filings of the last 30 days that have it, each opening the document, so you see how often the alert would fire. Then Add Alert. The first look only notes the company's latest filing. From then on, each new filing of those forms fires, the oldest first; with Once, only the first. The notification's Open Filing opens the document at the SEC in your browser, and the alert keeps the second EDGAR accepted the filing. Without Contains, several companies and industries are looked for in EDGAR's latest filings, which go back about a day: filings made while Pollis is closed for longer are missed. With it, the full-text search goes back as far as needed, though it may index a filing some minutes after it is published.

In Explore > Access Data Libraries, Yahoo Finance and Alpha Vantage have Alert Me... beside their Symbol, US SEC EDGAR beside its CIK, FRED, ECB and IMF beside each tab's Series, and World Bank on its One Indicator tab: it opens Add Alert with the symbol, company or series filled in.

Explore > Alerts lists Your Alerts, each with its latest value and period or latest filing, and Pause, Resume and Remove; a quote opens its Quote page, with your alerts drawn across the chart, and a filing alert opens the company's page at EDGAR. Fired Alerts lists what fired, with the value before and after, the band it left for a statistical condition, or the filing and Open Filing; Mark Read and Mark All Read clear them. The welcome page has an Alerts tab beside RSS with the same. Alerts are kept in ~/.pollis/alerts/alerts.json (Open alerts.json), and fired alerts in history.jsonl beside it. With several windows open, only one of them looks things up. Event studies The filings an alert fires can be the events of a study of how the stock moved around them: Start Event Study on the alert, or Auto Event Study when you add it (Event Studies, page ). Yahoo Finance does not know …, or could not be reached & Check the symbol at Yahoo Finance's site, as it is written there (^GSPC, BZ=F), and the internet connection. The SEC does not know …, or could not be reached & Try the CIK instead of the ticker: some filers have no ticker in the SEC's list. Check the internet connection. Needs your SEC contact & Set Contact on the Add Alert page, under SEC Filings: a name and an email address. Needs your FRED key & Set FRED Key on the Add Alert page, under Economic Data. Needs Julia & A statistical condition is computed in Julia: install it (Install Julia, page ), and the alert goes on. Julia is installing OnlineStats.jl & The first time only; the alert is checked again within the minute. An alert fired late & Quotes are delayed by up to about 20 minutes, filings are looked at every 15 minutes and series every hour; nothing is looked up while Pollis is closed.

How stocks move around SEC filings, and rates, yields and stocks around the FOMC's releases, a minute at a time; and how an outcome moves when units are treated at different times. An event study measures how something moves around events. A market event study follows prices in the minutes around them: the SEC filings an alert fires, with the minute prices of each filer's stock and of a benchmark; or the FOMC's releases, with federal funds and SOFR futures, Treasury yields, TIPS and the S&P 500. While Pollis is open it captures the prices from Yahoo Finance as they come and draws the result on the page. A panel event study follows an outcome over the years, quarters or months after units are treated at different times: states adopting a policy, firms a rule, or the clinics of a stepped-wedge trial crossing from control to treatment one group after another, from a table of your own. Either way the study is a folder that a notebook analyses with EventStudies.jl.

An alert on SEC filings chooses the events: its companies, forms, 8-K items and words (Alerts, page ). Add Alert... on the page makes one. Model > Event Studies, New Study: a Title, Kind Market Event Study, Events SEC Filings, and the alert. Benchmark: a Yahoo Finance symbol, ^GSPC for the S&P 500 at first. Normal Return: Market-Adjusted takes the benchmark's return out; Market Model takes out alpha plus beta times it, estimated on the minute returns of the regular sessions of the Estimation Days before the period. Event Time: First Public, the earlier of the company's newswire release and EDGAR's acceptance, as results are often on the wires hours before the 8-K; or EDGAR Acceptance alone. Periods: minutes Before and After the event, at first 30 and 120; Next Open also follows an event outside the regular session from the next open. Add Period adds another. Then Make Study. A new study starts with the filings the alert would have fired in the last 30 days, as Yahoo Finance keeps minute prices for 30 days, and adds each filing the alert fires from then on. On the alert, Start Event Study opens this page with the alert chosen, and Auto Event Study starts a study with the settings above the first time the alert fires.

For each filing, Pollis looks for the company's release on GlobeNewswire, Business Wire, PR Newswire or ACCESS Newswire from a day before EDGAR accepted it to a day after: in Google News, and in PR Newswire's own feeds, which Pollis reads every 10 minutes while there is a study of filings and which give the time to the second (Media Coverage, page ). The events show the Release, the Accepted time and the Lead of one over the other; News opens Media Coverage around the event.

New Study, Market Event Study, FOMC Releases: which releases are events (the statement, the Summary of Economic Projections, the minutes, other), and the Instruments, by what their move tells: Target Rate Surprise (FF1, the current month's federal funds future), Path and Forward Guidance (FF2 to FF4, SOFR futures, the 2-year note future ZT) and Fed Information Effect (^FVX, ^TNX, TIP, ^GSPC, ES). The period is 10 Min Before, 20 After, the tight window of Gürkaynak, Sack and Swanson (2005). A new study starts with the releases of the last 59 days, with five-minute prices for those older than 30 days.

Your Studies lists each study, with its events and how many are still capturing prices. Open one: A study of filings draws the cumulative average abnormal return (CAAR), in per cent, with its 95% band, and each event's in grey, From the Event or From the Next Open; under it, the articles about the events. Events lists each filing: Company, Form, When (during the session, before the open or after the close), Prices and its CAR. A study of FOMC releases draws each instrument's average move from the start of the period, with its 95% band, in basis points for rates and yields and in per cent for prices, and lists the releases. Open Folder, Edit study.toml and Open Notebook.

Each study is a folder in ~/.pollis/event-studies: study.toml, its settings; events.csv, the events with their times in UTC; prices/, a file of bars per event; and, for filings, news/, the articles about each. Open Notebook opens study.ipynb, which installs EventStudies.jl from the Pollis registry and runs it on the folder: filings: for each period, the average and cumulative average abnormal returns a minute at a time with their t, the CAR's t, the Boehmer, Masumeci and Poulsen (1991) test, and abnormal volume; FOMC releases: each instrument's move at each release, the mean move with its t, and the mean move a minute at a time. The results are written to results/. Events still capturing prices count up to the last complete minute: run the notebook again as they come in. What it does not do Prices are captured only while Pollis is open; a study catches up on reopening within Yahoo Finance's 30 days of minute prices (60 of five-minute prices), and an event older than that has none. A filer without a ticker has no prices. An expired futures contract is gone from Yahoo Finance, so FF1 of a past month has none, and Yahoo Finance has no 2-year yield in minutes: ZT stands for it, as a price. No alert on SEC filings yet & Add Alert... on the page, with Alert On set to SEC Filings. No prices at Yahoo Finance & The stock did not trade around the event, or Yahoo Finance does not list it. Older than the 30 days of minute prices & The event came before what Yahoo Finance keeps: it stays in the events, without prices. Some are not among the events & The last 30 days had more filings than EDGAR's full-text search reads: narrow the alert.

A panel study is made from a table of your own rather than from prices Pollis captures, and nothing happens until its notebook runs. New Study: a Title and Kind Panel Event Study. Table, Choose File...: a CSV file with a row per unit and time (or per individual, unit and time). Its columns and first rows are shown, and it is copied into the study's folder as panel.csv. Times are whole numbers: years, or quarters or months numbered in order. Columns: the Unit (also the clusters of the standard errors), the Time and the Outcome. Treated: a Treatment Indicator, not 0 from the time a unit is treated, or a First Treated column, the time each unit is first treated, missing or 0 for never. Choose each one: what a column means cannot be read from its name, and a column called treat may only say which units are ever treated.
